sections.overview: Apis nigrocincta is a cavity-nesting honey bee native to Southeast Asia. It is part of the Asian cavity-nesting honey-bee group and is especially associated with the Philippines and nearby Indonesian islands. The species has received less biological study than the widely managed western honey bee, so many details of its ecology remain poorly known.
sections.identification: It is a social honey bee with the familiar three-part insect body, two pairs of wings, pollen-carrying hind legs in workers and a banded abdomen. Its forewings measure about 7–9 mm; a reliable range for whole-body length has not been documented, and no sex-specific body-size figures were found. Identification within Asian cavity-nesting Apis is difficult from appearance alone: researchers use a combination of morphology, nest traits and genetic evidence to separate close species. A photograph without locality or close diagnostic detail may therefore be insufficient for confident identification. No reliable adult body-mass figure or sex-specific mass difference was found in the consulted species sources.
sections.habitat: Published accounts place the species in the Philippines and Indonesia, including Sulawesi and the Sangihe Islands. It nests in enclosed cavities rather than building the exposed single-comb nests characteristic of some other honey bees. Available sources provide a regional distribution, but do not establish a complete, fine-scale map of occupied habitats.
sections.diet: Like other honey bees, workers collect floral nectar and pollen to provision the colony. The species-specific studies retrieved for this profile focus on distribution, nesting and relationships among Asian honey bees; they do not provide a detailed, quantified account of its preferred flowers or seasonal diet.
sections.behavior: The species lives in colonies and uses cavity nests. Research on Asian cavity-nesting honey bees distinguishes A. nigrocincta from close relatives through nest and brood-cell characteristics as well as genetic markers. Detailed field observations of its foraging, swarming and communication are sparse in the sources reviewed here.
sections.reproduction: Colony reproduction in honey bees involves production of new queens and the departure of a queen with workers to establish another colony. For A. nigrocincta, the sources used here do not provide a well-supported species-specific schedule, mating range or colony-founding rate, so those values are not supplied.
sections.ecology: As a native social bee, A. nigrocincta visits flowering plants and can contribute to pollination. Its cavity-nesting biology makes suitable nest sites part of its habitat requirements. The reviewed research emphasizes how little is known about the ecology and conservation of several Asian honey bees; it does not quantify this species’ pollination contribution or population trend.
sections.conservation: No current global Red List category or population trend was confirmed in the sources used for this account. The absence of a verified status should not be read as evidence that the species is secure; the research literature specifically notes substantial knowledge gaps for Asian honey bees.
